attributes.action: Police powers to seize a vehicle after the driver has been caught drink driving
attributes.additional_details: The current law is that police officers have no powers to remove/seize a vehicle after the driver has been arrested for drink driving instead they have to leave the vehicle in situ for when the driver has been released from custody. Insurance companies should amend their policies to state that if you are caught drink driving your insurance is invalid which then leads to officers having the power to seize the vehicle under section 165 no insurance
attributes.background: My petition is for the police to have the power to seize a vehicle after the driver has been caught drink driving and over the limit instead of leaving the vehicle in situ for the offender to return to and drive the vehicle away potentially after drinking again

rejection.details:
The police already has such powers. More information:

https://www.gov.uk/stopped-by-police-while-driving-your-rights/when-the-police-can-seize-your-vehicle

"The police can seize a vehicle if they think it’s being used in a way that causes alarm, harassment or distress, for example careless or inconsiderate driving."

https://policing.uk/know-your-rights/can-police-take-your-car-keys
